derivation_notes: The constant-hazard clearance law is refined so that the effective removal hazard from the contagious class increases with current contagious occupancy, representing burden-dependent self-isolation, detection, or faster loss from the counted contagious state at higher C. When contagious_clearance_burden approaches zero, the departure term continuously reduces to the parent linear clearance law.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that contagious departure is exactly first-order in C by introducing a burden-dependent clearance factor in the C loss term. This preserves the same staged inflow structure while creating stronger downward curvature in dC_dt at higher contagious occupancy.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Departure from contagiousness is a time-independent first-order loss term clearance_rate*C with no occupancy dependence.
assumption_audit.mechanism: At high contagious burden, symptom recognition, self-isolation, clinical removal, or rapid depletion of highly shedding individuals can make effective departure from the counted contagious class accelerate with C rather than remain exactly linear.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when contagious_clearance_burden = 0, giving the original loss term clearance_rate*C.

response_change.parent_relation: The inflow to C is proportional to P with a single feedback-suppressed gain, so at fixed C the target mapping dC_dt versus P is linear and the loss term is exactly proportional to C.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same stage-flow structure but relax the idealized constant clearance hazard so that departure from C depends nonlinearly on contagious burden, making dC_dt bend downward more strongly at higher C even when P is unchanged.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar P but different C, the decline and post-peak decay of C become disproportionately faster at larger C; the parent can only scale this loss linearly with one shared clearance parameter.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when contagious occupancy reaches moderate to high levels so that burden-dependent departure is non-negligible relative to baseline linear clearance, while P remains positive or recently declining during the peak and decay window.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early growth at low C still resembles the parent because clearance is near-linear; in holdout regimes with larger peak C or slower presymptomatic depletion, the stronger high-C downturn and sharper post-peak decay reveal the changed curvature.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent in the limit of vanishing burden dependence in contagious departure, where clearance becomes effectively proportional to C over the observed range.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: burden-accelerated departure from the contagious compartment
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: At high contagious burden, symptom recognition, self-isolation, clinical removal, or rapid depletion of highly shedding individuals can make effective departure from the counted contagious class accelerate with C rather than remain exactly linear.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the loss law now depends jointly on clearance_rate and the state C, changing the shape of the target mapping across occupancy levels rather than merely rescaling it.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Departure from contagiousness is a time-independent first-order loss term clearance_rate*C with no occupancy dependence.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Departure from contagiousness has a burden-accelerated hazard, with effective loss growing with contagious occupancy.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting contagious_clearance_burden = 0 exactly recovers the parent target equation.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compared at times or parameter settings where presymptomatic inflow pressure is similar but C differs, the child produces nearly parent-like behavior at low C and increasingly stronger negative dC_dt at higher C, yielding a lower earlier peak and sharper post-peak decay. This is a changed target mapping, not only an auxiliary-trajectory change, because the scored C equation itself gains an explicit quadratic-in-C loss contribution.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent clearance_rate cannot reproduce both low-C near-linear clearance and high-C accelerated loss across these conditions, because the parent loss term is strictly proportional to C. Retuning existing parent parameters can shift overall timing and scale, but it cannot create the added high-C downward curvature in the scored mapping without over-altering low-C behavior.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when contagious occupancy reaches moderate to high levels so that burden-dependent departure is non-negligible relative to baseline linear clearance, while P remains positive or recently declining during the peak and decay window.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early growth at low C still resembles the parent because clearance is near-linear; in holdout regimes with larger peak C or slower presymptomatic depletion, the stronger high-C downturn and sharper post-peak decay reveal the changed curvature.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent in the limit of vanishing burden dependence in contagious departure, where clearance becomes effectively proportional to C over the observed range.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes each contagious individual leaves the contagious state with the same constant hazard regardless of how crowded the contagious compartment is.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Departure from contagiousness is a time-independent first-order loss term clearance_rate*C with no occupancy dependence.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: At high contagious burden, symptom recognition, self-isolation, clinical removal, or rapid depletion of highly shedding individuals can make effective departure from the counted contagious class accelerate with C rather than remain exactly linear.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the constant-clearance assumption rather than add another hidden stage. The parent target mapping is dC_dt = inflow(P,C) - clearance_rate*C, so for fixed P it has one fixed negative slope in C from the explicit loss term, with only the existing inflow feedback contributing additional curvature. Vary condition by trajectories that reach different contagious burdens because of different admissible parameter settings or observed state combinations, while holding the same model form and one shared parameter set. Then compare times where P is similar but C differs: the child predicts extra downward bending of dC_dt at larger C through burden-accelerated departure, giving a lower and earlier peak and a steeper late decline. The parent cannot reproduce that specific high-C loss curvature with a single shared clearance_rate because changing clearance_rate rescales loss equally at low and high C. This is observable under the existing initial-condition contract because C starts at zero and can rise substantially from the staged latent reservoir; the effect is weak if C stays small throughout observation, in which case the child should reduce continuously back toward the parent.

scenario_text: Track a cohort of already infected people as they pass from a latent state into a contagious state and then cease being contagious. No new infections enter the cohort during observation, so the dynamics isolate disease-stage progression from transmission. The target is the rate of change of the contagious group, which reflects both arrivals from latency and departures from contagiousness. Constant progression and clearance hazards produce a delayed peak in contagious prevalence.
